# Colormeris agent reference

Prompts, limits, caching and design notes live in the code and CLAUDE.md: [prompts](../src/agent/llm.ts) ([decision mode](../src/agent/decide/prompt.ts)), [schemas](../src/agent/schema.ts), [runner](../src/agent/runner.ts).

`window.colormeris` ([api.ts](../src/agent/api.ts)): `await colormeris.run(name, args)` validates against the JSON Schema, never throws, returns `{ok, result, state?, notes?}` or `{ok: false, error}`. `batch([{name, args}])` stops at the first failure; `tools()` lists schemas; `log()` returns the action and decision logs. Coordinates are page pixels. `panelId` (optional, default: active panel) is accepted by panel actions. * = required. _LLM._ = also a tool of the heatmap agent's LLM.

## Reading

### `get_state`
Snapshot of the source, panels, calibration and readiness. Cheap; call after every mutation. _LLM._

### `get_results`
Extracted values of a panel: heatmap matrix with ΔE and flags, or ROI region statistics. _LLM._

### `get_questions`
Open typed questions (decisions) about the current project, with evidence and answer schemas.

### `sample_pixel`
Color at a point, its CIELAB value and, when the colorbar is calibrated, the matched value and ΔE. _LLM._
- `x`* number: Page pixel.
- `y`* number: Page pixel.
- `radius` integer (≥ 0, ≤ 20): Average a (2r+1)² square. Default 0.

### `focus`
Zoom the viewer to points (for screenshot-based checking).
- `points`* {x, y}[]

## File, tool and page

### `open_url`
Open a PDF, PNG, JPG or project zip by URL (same origin or CORS-enabled). _Mutates._
- `url`* string

### `set_tool`
Switch between the heatmap and ROI tools. _Mutates._
- `tool`* "heatmap" \\| "roi"

### `go_to_page`
Show a PDF page (1-based). _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `page`* integer (≥ 1)

### `select_panel`
Make a panel active. _Mutates._ _LLM._

### `add_panel`
Add a panel on the current page for the active tool and make it active. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `name` string

### `rename_panel`
Rename a panel. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `name`* string

### `remove_panel`
Delete a panel with its calibration and review. The last panel of a page is replaced by an empty one. Undo restores it. _Mutates._

## Grid

### `set_grid`
Place the grid by its outer top-left and bottom-right corners, or by 4 corners (TL, TR, BR, BL) for skewed scans. Rows and columns are filled in automatically from the colors inside the grid, and a confirm_grid_size question opens. Precision matters: a few pixels off shifts every cell. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `topLeft` {x, y}: Outer top-left corner of the top-left cell. Give with bottomRight.
- `bottomRight` {x, y}: Outer bottom-right corner of the bottom-right cell. Give with topLeft.
- `corners` {x, y}[]: Instead of topLeft/bottomRight: all 4 outer corners, in order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left.

### `detect_grid_size`
Guess rows and columns from the colors inside the placed grid, with confidences (below ~1.3 is uncertain). Does not change the panel. _LLM._

### `set_grid_size`
Set rows and columns. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `rows`* integer (≥ 1, ≤ 1000): Number of cell rows.
- `cols`* integer (≥ 1, ≤ 1000): Number of cell columns.

### `set_labels`
Row, column and (ROI) box labels. Give at least one list. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `rows` string[]: Row labels, top to bottom.
- `cols` string[]: Column labels, left to right.
- `boxes` string[]: ROI box names in reading order.

### `remove_grid`
Remove the grid. _Mutates._ _LLM._

## Colorbar and matching

### `set_colorbar`
Place the colorbar along its colored strip. With snap (default), the line is moved to the strip's centre line, both ends go to its first and last colored pixel (off the outline) and halfWidth is set from the strip width; the result reports what moved. Existing ticks stay at their page positions. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `start`* {x, y}: One end of the colored strip, on its centre line. Just inside the border: the first pixel that shows the color, not the outline.
- `end`* {x, y}: The other end, on the centre line, just inside the border (not on the outline).
- `halfWidth` number (≥ 0, ≤ 50): Pixels averaged on each side of the line. Set from the strip when snapping; keep it inside the strip.
- `snap` boolean: Snap the line and its ends to the colored strip under it. Default true; set false only when a snap was clearly wrong.

### `add_tick`
Add a labelled tick on the placed colorbar. Give its position ONE way: `at` (the page point of the tick mark, projected onto the bar; preferred) or `t` (0 at start, 1 at end). With snap (default), it moves to the nearest tick mark beside the strip within a few pixels; the result says how far. Example: {"at": {"x": 606, "y": 822}, "value": 3}. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `at` {x, y}: Page point of the tick mark. Use this or t, not both.
- `t` number (≥ -0.1, ≤ 1.1): Position along the bar, 0 at start and 1 at end. Use this or at, not both.
- `value`* number: The printed tick label as a number, with any ×10^n multiplier applied (e.g. 1.4e9).
- `snap` boolean: Snap to the nearest tick mark. Default true; set false for bars without tick marks or when the snap picked the wrong mark.

### `set_tick_value`
Change a tick's value. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `tickId`* string: From add_tick or get_state.
- `value`* number

### `remove_tick`
Remove a tick. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `tickId`* string: From add_tick or get_state.

### `set_colorbar_scale`
linear; log10 when the tick labels are raw numbers on a logarithmic bar; piecewise (or piecewise-log10 for positive values over decades) when the tick values are uneven along the bar, e.g. a binned bar labelled 1e4, 2e4, 2e5 at its steps: values are interpolated between neighbouring ticks only. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `scale`* "linear" \\| "log10" \\| "piecewise" \\| "piecewise-log10"

### `set_settings`
Matching settings. _Mutates._ _LLM._
- `distance` "de2000" \\| "de76"
- `maxDeltaE` number (≥ 0)
- `grayChroma` number (≥ 0)
- `sampleFraction` number (≥ 0.05, ≤ 1)

## ROI regions

### `add_region`
ROI: add a region in image pixels. ellipse/rect use {cx, cy, rx, ry} (rect rx/ry are half-extents); polygon uses {points}. With replicate (default) and a grid, it is copied into every box. _Mutates._
- `shape`* "ellipse" \\| "rect" \\| "polygon"
- `geom`* {cx, cy, rx, ry, points}
- `name` string
- `replicate` boolean

### `remove_region`
ROI: remove a region and all its copies. _Mutates._
- `regionId`* string

### `set_scale_bar`
ROI: a known distance between two points, for areas in real units. _Mutates._
- `p1`* {x, y}
- `p2`* {x, y}
- `length`* number (> 0)
- `unit` "cm" \\| "mm"

## Decisions and review

### `answer_question`
Answer a question from get_questions. Answers below the policy confidence are logged and left for a human. _Mutates._
- `questionId`* string
- `answer`* any: Must match the question's answerSchema.
- `confidence` number (≥ 0, ≤ 1)
- `source` string: Who decided, e.g. "claude", "human".
- `model` string

### `set_review`
Record a review of a panel's current extraction: accepted or rejected (with an optional note on what is wrong), or null to clear it. A rejected panel stays marked until it is accepted or its values change. _Mutates._
- `status`* "accepted" \\| "rejected" \\| null
- `note` string
- `source` string

## History and export

### `undo`
Undo the last change. _Mutates._ _LLM._

### `redo`
Redo. _Mutates._ _LLM._

### `export_project`
Download the project zip (includes agent/decisions.json).

## Typed questions

`get_questions` lists decisions (`id`, `type`, `panelId`, `prompt`, `evidence`, `answerSchema`); `answer_question` answers with `confidence` and `source`. Answers below `policy.minConfidence` (0.9) are escalated, not applied; `source: "human"` always applies.

- `confirm_grid_size` → `{rows, cols}`
- `classify_flagged` (≤ 3 flagged cells) → `keep` | `exclude` | `recheck_colorbar`
- `classify_flagged_cells` (> 3) → `keep_all` | `exclude_all` | `recheck_colorbar`
- `confirm_tick_order` → `as_placed` | `fix_needed`
- `confirm_extraction` → `accept` | `reject` (sets `panel.review`; goes `stale` when values change)

## Runner tools (agent only mode)

### `view_page`
Image of the current page (or a region of it) with pixel rulers. overlay "calibration" draws the grids, colorbars and ticks of this page's panels; "reconstruction" repaints each cell with the color its extracted value maps to.
- `region` {x0, y0, x1, y1}: Area to show, in page pixels. Omit for the whole page.
- `overlay` "none" \\| "calibration" \\| "reconstruction"

### `view_pages_overview`
Thumbnails of up to 12 PDF pages in one image, labelled with page numbers, to find the pages with heatmaps.
- `from`* integer (≥ 1)
- `to`* integer (≥ 1)

### `finish`
End the run with a short summary for the user.
- `summary`* string

## Decision-mode tools (LLM actions: `go_to_page`, `select_panel`, `rename_panel`, `remove_panel`, `set_labels`, `set_colorbar`, `add_tick`, `remove_tick`, `set_colorbar_scale`, `undo`; models: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` + `typesafe/jev-1.14`)

### `locate_heatmap`
Find one heatmap with the decision model and calibrate a panel for it: the grid on its cells (rows and columns counted by the app) and its colorbar. Uses a new panel unless panelId is given or the active panel is still empty. Returns the placement and an image with numbered tick-label boxes, or lettered colorbar candidates when it cannot tell which colorbar is this heatmap's.
- `name`* string: Figure label, e.g. "Fig 2f". Becomes the panel name.
- `description`* string: What singles this heatmap out on the page: panel letter, title, position, first row label.
- `box` {x0, y0, x1, y1}: Only when a first locate found the wrong heatmap: the cells' rough extent in page pixels, read from the page image's rulers. The decision model is not asked; each edge moves at most a few px onto the cells' edge.

### `set_ticks`
Set the colorbar ticks (replaces the panel's ticks), then check the extraction; returns the check and an image of the ticks. Give each tick by its numbered tick-label box (mark), or, when the boxes are missing or wrong, by its place along the colored strip (t). Ticks snap to tick marks. Unless you give a scale, the app picks one that fits: for a binned colorbar, and piecewise for evenly stepped labels at uneven places along a smooth bar.
- `ticks`* {mark, t, value}[]
- `scale` "linear" \\| "log10" \\| "piecewise" \\| "piecewise-log10": Leave out unless the labels grow by constant factors (log10). piecewise: uneven tick values interpolated between neighbours.

### `use_colorbar`
Give a panel its colorbar: one of the lettered candidates from locate_heatmap (candidate), the colorbar of another panel with its ticks and scale (fromPanel: blocks sharing one colorbar), or a strip at a rough box in page pixels (box) when none was found. Returns numbered tick-label boxes for set_ticks (except with fromPanel, which checks the panel).
- `candidate` string: Letter of a colorbar candidate, e.g. "B".
- `fromPanel` string: Id of a panel whose colorbar this heatmap shares.
- `box` {x0, y0, x1, y1}: The colored strip's rough extent in page pixels, from the page rulers.

### `correct_grid_size`
Correct the app's row and column count of a panel when the image shows it is wrong: magenta lines that merge or split cells, or a strip without cell borders. Count cell edges in the image; count labels only where there are no edges (one label can cover several replicate cells). With box (the cells' rough extent from the page rulers) the grid's outer edges also move onto the cells (at most a few px each); without it the corners stay. Then checks the extraction.
- `rows`* integer (≥ 1, ≤ 500)
- `cols`* integer (≥ 1, ≤ 500)
- `reason`* string: What in the image shows the count, e.g. "3 replicate cells under each column label".
- `box` {x0, y0, x1, y1}: Only when the outer grid lines miss the cells: the cells' rough extent in page pixels.

### `check_printed`
Cross-check a calibrated panel against numbers printed in its cells: give 3–5 cells spread over the heatmap (with the lowest and highest printed numbers) and the numbers as printed. The app compares them with the values it extracted from the colors and says whether they agree; a disagreement that grows with the value or shifts all of them points at wrong tick values or colorbar ends. The colors stay the values.
- `cells`* {row, col, value}[]

### `check_panel`
Check a panel again: whether it is ready, whether its tick values fit the scale, and how many cells are far from the colorbar's colors, off it or past its ends.

### `ask`
Ask the decision model your own questions about one region of the current page (no rulers in its image). Box answers come back in page pixels. Use it rarely, for one heatmap at a time.
- `region` {x0, y0, x1, y1}: Area in page pixels. Omit for the whole page.
- `overlay` "none" \\| "calibration" \\| "reconstruction"
- `questions`* object: Up to 6 questions by id: {id: {type, instructions, criteria}}.
